slides.headline: Sam Altman says OpenAI *will build a humanoid robot*. He expects a demo in 2027

slides.heading: Two words: *"We will"*
paras: On the Sources podcast, Altman was asked if OpenAI would build a humanoid robot. His answer: "We will."
He said the human shape makes sense because "the world is very much designed for people," so "matching that form factor seems good."

slides.heading: The *brain* is the hard part
paras: Altman says the robot's looks are "less important than really figuring out ... the brain that makes the robot work."
OpenAI has tried robotics before. Its Dactyl project trained a robot hand in simulation, and the same approach was later used to solve a Rubik's Cube.

slides.heading: A demo in *2027*
paras: Altman told Fortune he expects "a cool demo in 2027," but said robots will not be walking the streets for a few years after that.
OpenAI's careers page lists 27 robotics openings, from custom actuators and motion control to manufacturing and supply chain.

slides.heading: Joining a *crowded race*
paras: The first goal is general purpose robots that help skilled workers build infrastructure. A personal robot is the long term aim.

paras.t: Tesla has worked on Optimus for years and XPENG has its IRON humanoid. OpenAI has shared no price, design or release date.

image.credit: Kevin Frayer / Getty Images via Engadget

slides.hook: OpenAI wants a robot in every home. Follow to see the 2027 demo the day it lands.
